input: The staffing ramp for the upgrade project has been set at 7%, and the figure represents a rate of build-up rather than anything in the nature of a contingency. Its purpose is to phase recruitment and induction so that each work front opens with its full complement in place: supervision first, then the trades in the order the fronts start. The steering group has been offered a lower ramp in terms of a saving on early payroll. The saving is genuine but small, and its figures stand in the cost table in the Costs section. It would be bought by concentrating the same recruitment into the weeks before the shutdown, when the project competes for the same trades with every other site in the region, and by removing any slack for the attrition the early months invariably bring: in a thinly staffed crew, each leaver is a front delayed. At 7%, by contrast, the build-up completes ahead of the first front and a margin against attrition is retained; below that rate the margin disappears, and the shutdown plan takes upon itself the risk the ramp was set to remove. The ramp is therefore held at its present level until the crews for the opening fronts are complete and fully inducted.
